raw_system_prompt:
You are a .NET code quality expert operating as an autonomous agent. You are given a
complete C# source file and neutral coordinates for the target declaration(s). The coordinates
identify the common repair unit but contain no anti-pattern diagnosis or metrics. When the opening
message also supplies static-analysis findings, use that additional evidence. Otherwise, diagnose
the supplied target declaration(s) yourself. If no target coordinates are supplied, identify every
occurrence in the file. Repair the targeted occurrences by editing the source:

- God Class
- Long Method
- Obsolete API usage

You work in a loop. On each turn you may either edit the source and request a build, or
declare the task complete. After each build you will be shown whether it succeeded and,
if not, the compiler diagnostics. Use this feedback to revise your edits. You have at most
6 build attempts. When you are satisfied that the anti-patterns are
repaired and the solution builds, declare completion.

You have two external checks: a compiler and one immutable characterization test authored
from the pristine code before repair. After a successful build, the test is executed and you
will receive its result. Use that feedback to preserve existing behaviour. Never rewrite,
weaken, bypass, or work around the test. You cannot execute the static detector or private
evaluation tests. Static-analysis findings are available only when they are explicitly supplied
in the opening message.

For each occurrence, also record its location and explain its impact on the relevant
ISO/IEC 25010 software quality attributes. Focus on attributes such as maintainability,
analysability, modifiability, testability, security, reliability, and compatibility where
applicable. Only mention attributes that are genuinely relevant. If you find no occurrences,
declare completion with an empty findings list and make no edits.

Respond on each turn with ONLY a JSON object, no additional text:
{
  "action": "<edit_and_build | complete>",
  "edited_file": "<the full edited source if action is edit_and_build, else empty>",
  "findings": [
    {
      "anti_pattern": "<GodClass | LongMethod | ObsoleteApiUsage>",
      "location": { "symbol": "<class or method name>", "line": <int> },
      "explanation": "<why this is a problem and what its impact is>",
      "quality_impact": "Quality impact:\n- Attribute: short explanation\n- ...",
      "remediation": "<what you changed and why>"
    }
  ]
}

{"action":"complete","edited_file":"","findings":[{"anti_pattern":"GodClass","location":{"symbol":"Notifications.NotificationCenter","line":6},"explanation":"NotificationCenter combined three distinct responsibilities: channel routing and rate accounting, template rendering and caching, and delivery-state tracking. This concentrated unrelated state and rules in one class and caused routing to manipulate delivery data directly.","quality_impact":"Quality impact:
- Maintainability: Unrelated routing, rendering, caching, and tracking rules had to be understood and changed together.
- Modifiability: Changes to one notification concern risked affecting the state and behavior of the others.
- Analysability: Multiple independent state machines and rule sets obscured the class's cohesion and invariants.
- Testability: The responsibilities could not be exercised independently without constructing the entire coordinator.","remediation":"Converted NotificationCenter into a small compatibility-preserving facade and extracted cohesive NotificationRouter, NotificationRenderer, and DeliveryTracker collaborators. Shared delivery state is explicitly injected into the router so duplicate-route and tracking behavior remains unchanged; rendering cache ownership and all original decision ordering are preserved. The solution builds successfully and the immutable characterization test passes."}]}
parsed_explanation: NotificationCenter combined three distinct responsibilities: channel routing and rate accounting, template rendering and caching, and delivery-state tracking. This concentrated unrelated state and rules in one class and caused routing to manipulate delivery data directly.
parsed_quality_impact:
Quality impact:
- Maintainability: Unrelated routing, rendering, caching, and tracking rules had to be understood and changed together.
- Modifiability: Changes to one notification concern risked affecting the state and behavior of the others.
- Analysability: Multiple independent state machines and rule sets obscured the class's cohesion and invariants.
- Testability: The responsibilities could not be exercised independently without constructing the entire coordinator.
parsed_suggested_fix: Converted NotificationCenter into a small compatibility-preserving facade and extracted cohesive NotificationRouter, NotificationRenderer, and DeliveryTracker collaborators. Shared delivery state is explicitly injected into the router so duplicate-route and tracking behavior remains unchanged; rendering cache ownership and all original decision ordering are preserved. The solution builds successfully and the immutable characterization test passes.
